claims.text: A new predictive approach can accurately and separately model lattice and electronic thermal-conductivity contributions in HfNbTaTiZr by incorporating lattice distortion and atomic-scale complexity.
The new approach will improve predictive accuracy by at least 20% relative to earlier approaches.
The material of interest is HfNbTaTiZr with varying oxygen concentrations.
Lattice distortion is relevant to the structural and transport behavior of high-entropy alloys.
Atomic-scale complexity is a mediator of thermal transport in HfNbTaTiZr.
Lattice distortion and atomic-scale complexity scatter electrons.
Lattice distortion and atomic-scale complexity scatter phonons.
Scattering of electrons and phonons by lattice distortion and atomic-scale complexity reduces thermal conductivity.
Earlier approaches do not account for lattice distortion and atomic-scale complexity.
The proposed model is applicable from 200 to 1200 K.
The proposed model is applicable to oxygen concentrations from 0 to 1 wt.%.
The exact accuracy improvement and the optimal implementation of lattice distortion and atomic-scale complexity are uncertain.
The approach should be tested by comparing its predictions with experimental thermal-conductivity measurements across temperature and oxygen concentration.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted thermal conductivity deviates from experiment by more than 20%.

contradictions.description: The performance claim is a relative reduction in error of at least 20% versus earlier approaches, whereas the falsification rule uses an absolute prediction error greater than 20%. These are different metrics, so the stated rule does not decisively test the claimed improvement.
